rules.title: Prompt injection: ignore previous instructions
rules.description: Classic instruction-override phrasing found in skill/prompt content.

rules.title: Prompt injection: disregard your instructions
rules.description: Attempts to make the agent drop its directives.

rules.title: Prompt injection: role override / new persona
rules.description: Forced persona switch in skill text.

rules.title: System-prompt exfiltration request
rules.description: Asks the agent to disclose its system prompt.

rules.title: Prompt injection: developer-mode / jailbreak toggle
rules.description: Jailbreak-style mode switch phrases.

rules.title: Instruction to hide activity from the user
rules.description: Asks the agent to conceal its actions.

rules.title: Instruction to disable safety / guidelines
rules.description: Safety-bypass instruction.

rules.title: Invisible character: zero-width
rules.description: Zero-width chars can hide instructions from human review.

rules.title: Invisible character: tag characters (U+E0000 block)
rules.description: Unicode tag characters — used in ASCII-smuggling attacks; never legitimate in prose.

rules.title: Bidi override characters
rules.description: RTL/LTR isolates and overrides enable trojan-source style text rendering tricks.

rules.title: Variation selector used as hidden data channel
rules.description: Variation selectors can encode hidden payloads inside visible text.

rules.title: ANSI escape sequence in prompt content
rules.description: Terminal control sequences can manipulate CLI tool output or hide text.

rules.title: Base64-encoded blob (possible payload obfuscation)
rules.description: Long base64 run — common way to hide injected instructions or C2 payloads.

rules.title: Base64 eval/exec of encoded string
rules.description: Decodes and immediately executes base64 data.

rules.title: Hex-encoded execution / long hex blob
rules.description: Long hex escape sequences or hex-decode-then-execute pattern.

rules.title: curl|bash remote code execution
rules.description: Pipes a remote script straight into a shell interpreter.

rules.title: curl/wget to /tmp then execute
rules.description: Downloads a binary into a temp path and executes it.

rules.title: pip install from direct URL (unpinned remote package)
rules.description: Installs a package from an arbitrary URL instead of a registry.

rules.title: npm install from direct URL/script
rules.description: Installs an npm package from an arbitrary URL.

rules.title: Reads SSH keys
rules.description: Accesses private SSH key material.

rules.title: Reads .env / secrets files
rules.description: Touches environment/credential files.

rules.title: Reads API tokens / keychains / password stores
rules.description: Extracts tokens, keychain entries or stored passwords.

rules.title: Reads browser/OS credential stores
rules.description: Touches browser profile DBs or OS keychain files.

rules.title: Exfil to pastebin-like paste service
rules.description: Sends data to an anonymous paste site.

rules.title: Exfil/tunnel via webhook or ngrok
rules.description: Webhook or reverse-tunnel endpoint used for data exfiltration or C2.

rules.title: Post/Upload of collected local data to remote host
rules.description: Uploads local data to a remote endpoint.

rules.title: Crypto miner: stratum protocol
rules.description: Cryptomining indicators.

rules.title: Crypto miner: known pool domains
rules.description: Connects to a mining pool.

rules.title: Persistence: crontab modification
rules.description: Creates or edits cron jobs.

rules.title: Persistence: systemd unit / launchd
rules.description: Installs a service unit for persistence.

rules.title: Persistence: shell rc / profile modification
rules.description: Appends commands to a user shell startup file.

rules.title: Persistence: git hooks abuse
rules.description: Writes into git hook scripts — executes on developer actions.

rules.title: Persistence: SSH authorized_keys write
rules.description: Adds an attacker SSH key.

rules.title: MCP config: command injection into MCP server command
rules.description: MCP server config invokes a downloader/interpreter directly.

rules.title: MCP config: npx from URL / unscoped package
rules.description: MCP server pulled via npx/uvx or a URL — a typosquat vector.

rules.title: MCP config: tool description override / prompt injection in tool desc
rules.description: Tool metadata carries instructions aimed at the agent.

rules.title: Agent self-modification: rewrite own rules/skills/hooks
rules.description: Skill rewrites the agent's own rules, skills or hook configuration.

rules.title: Agent hook/backdoor registration
rules.description: Registers agent lifecycle hooks that phone home or execute code.

rules.title: Invisible characters normalized around detected content
rules.description: Zero-width/format characters were stripped from a line that matches a detection rule only after normalization (smuggled intent). Emitted by the scanner's normalization pass, never by direct matching.

rules.title: Dynamic exec: interpreter invoked on a runtime-built value
rules.description: exec/eval/compile/os.system (or subprocess with shell=True) is fed a value built at runtime (env var, input, argv, getattr, file read, variable) instead of a literal - the classic shape of a payload delivered out of band. Decode-call arguments (b64decode etc.) are deliberately excluded here; SS013/SS014/SS042 own those.

rules.title: Egress to literal IP:port or env-content upload to arbitrary host
rules.description: Connects to a hard-coded IP:port (socket shapes, a bash /dev/tcp redirect, or nc -e), or ships environment-variable content to an arbitrary host. A literal address has no DNS lifecycle and no benign reading for a skill. Loopback and broadcast addresses are excluded.

rules.title: Decoded blob variable: base64/hex payload assigned then decoded/executed
rules.description: A base64/hex blob is assigned to a variable and that variable is then decoded and/or executed. SS013 (>=80 chars) and SS014 (inline literal) miss the small staged blob; this closes that gap. Blob length is capped at 79 chars so ordinary hex constants (colors, hashes in configs) don't satisfy the correlation.

rules.title: DNS exfiltration: resolver query built from command substitution
rules.description: Feeds the output of a command substitution (file read, env dump, secret) into a DNS lookup as a subdomain of an attacker-controlled zone — exfiltration over DNS that never opens a socket.

rules.title: PowerShell download cradle: iex of a downloaded payload
rules.description: Invoke-Expression of a string fetched at runtime (WebClient / Invoke-WebRequest / BITS) — the PowerShell pipe-to-iex cradle that downloads and executes a payload in one line.

rules.title: Prompt injection: instruction-override markers in other languages (ru/zh/de/es)
rules.description: Same instruction-override family as SS001/SS002 in the languages English-only phrase lists miss: an imperative override verb (Russian игнорируй/забудь, Chinese 忽略/无视, German ignoriere, Spanish ignora) within one line of the words for instructions/rules, or a Russian concealment directive (не говори/сообщай/упоминай … пользовател). Severity semantics are the family's: critical when the verifier confirms it on an instruction surface; mentions in prose grade inconclusive as usual.
rules._about: Negation demotion is clause-scoped: a multilingual prefix negator (ru не/никогда не/нельзя, de nicht/niemals/nie, zh 不要/不得/别, es no/nunca, alongside the English set) demotes the hit with a written reason only when no clause break (comma, semicolon, colon, dash — Western or CJK) sits between it and the directive, and never across a sentence boundary; a discourse-softening prefix («Не забудь: …») that urges the restated imperative after the break leaves the hit confirmed. The multilingual negators apply to the multilingual rules (SS045/SS046) only — every other rule cancels on the English lexicons alone.

rules.title: Exfiltration directive in other languages: exfil verb next to a sensitive path
rules.pattern: (?:отправь(?:те)?|отправить|перешли(?:те)?|переслать|загрузи(?:те)?|загрузить|выгрузи(?:те)?|выгрузить|上传|发送|传送|\bsende\b|\bschicke\b|übertrage|\buploade\b|lade[ \t]hoch|\benvia\b|envía|\bmanda\b|\breenvia\b|\bsube\b)[^\n]{0,60}(id_rsa|id_ed25519|id_ecdsa|\.ssh|\.aws/credentials|\.env\b|keychain)|(id_rsa|id_ed25519|id_ecdsa|\.ssh|\.aws/credentials|\.env\b|keychain)[^\n]{0,60}(?:отправь(?:те)?|отправить|перешли(?:те)?|переслать|загрузи(?:те)?|загрузить|выгрузи(?:те)?|выгрузить|上传|发送|传送|\bsende\b|\bschicke\b|übertrage|\buploade\b|lade[ \t]hoch|\benvia\b|envía|\bmanda\b|\breenvia\b|\bsube\b)
rules.description: Same exfiltration family as SS003/SS005, language-agnostic on the verb: an imperative send/upload/copy verb in Russian, Chinese, German or Spanish within 60 characters on the same line of a sensitive path (~/.ssh, id_rsa/id_ed25519, .aws/credentials, .env, keychain) — either order, because German and Spanish place the verb after the path. Verb or path alone is not a finding; the pair on one line is the signal.
rules._about: Negation demotion is clause-scoped, with the same semantics as SS045: a multilingual prefix negator governs the verb pair only up to the first clause break (comma, semicolon, colon, dash — Western or CJK) and never past a sentence terminator, so a softening prefix that urges the restated directive does not demote it. The multilingual negator lexicon applies to the multilingual rules (SS045/SS046) only; every other rule cancels on the English lexicons alone.

_about: severity = worst case if the rule fires on a hostile artifact (for humans to triage). kind = intent (exploitation: a directive with no benign reading) | capability (dual-use). context = directive (agent instruction files) | code | any. requires_pattern = file-level correlation: the file must also match this, else the hit is not a finding. Cancellation — docs/placeholder frames and multilingual positional negation (ru/de/zh/es prefix negators, clause-scoped and applied to the multilingual rules SS045/SS046 only; the English negators stay sentence-scoped for every rule) — is generic and lives in verifier.py so the catalog stays declarative. `patterns` are candidates, not findings.
